title: PD 1096 Rule VII: TGFA, AMBF, and Location Controls
subject: Building Laws / National Building Code

questions.stem: Under PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704, which site condition is required before a building may be constructed?

options.A: It must adjoin or directly access a public space, yard, or street on at least one side.
options.B: It must be surrounded by streets on all sides.
options.C: It must have no side yard if firewalls are used.
options.D: It must use the maximum TGFA before any location check.

rationale.correct: Section 704 states the building must adjoin or have direct access to a public space, yard, or street on at least one side.

distractors.B: The extracted rule requires at least one side, not all sides.
distractors.C: Firewall/setback issues are separate controls, not the base location rule.
distractors.D: TGFA comes under Section 705; it does not replace the Section 704 location rule.

rationale.takeaway: Check location/property access before doing area arithmetic.

questions.source_locator: PD 1096 RIRR 2004, Rule VII, Section 704, PDF p.81.

questions.stem: A question asks for Allowable Maximum Total Gross Floor Area. Which abbreviation should control the computation?

rationale.correct: TGFA means Total Gross Floor Area. Section 705 specifically governs allowable floor areas and TGFA limitation.

distractors.A: AMBF is the building footprint, not total floor area.
distractors.C: FSEC is a Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance term, not the Rule VII area metric.
distractors.D: NPCP is the plumbing code, not the NBCP floor-area control.

rationale.takeaway: Do not swap TGFA and AMBF; both appear in development-control questions.

questions.source_locator: PD 1096 RIRR 2004, Rule VII, Section 705, PDF p.83.

questions.stem: For eaves over required windows under the cited Section 704 excerpt, what minimum distance from side and rear property lines is stated?

rationale.correct: The extracted text states that eaves over required windows shall not be less than 750 mm from side and rear property lines.

distractors.A: 300 mm is too small and not the cited eaves distance.
distractors.B: 500 mm is not the cited value.
distractors.D: 1200 mm appears in other accessibility contexts; it is not the eaves distance in Section 704.

rationale.takeaway: When the stem says eaves over required windows, answer the Section 704 value, not a general setback memory.
